title: Dragonblight
body: The Dragonblight is the great white valley at the heart of southern Northrend, the place where dragons come when they are ready to die. Their bones lie across it in their thousands, and at its center rises Wyrmrest Temple, where the dragonflights meet in council under Alexstrasza the Life-Binder. The peace of that ancient graveyard is broken. Malygos's blue dragonflight is tearing at the ley lines of the land, and the Scourge raises frost wyrms from the old bones and digs at the grave of Galakrond. In the north, Angrathar the Wrathgate bars the way into Icecrown, and before it the Alliance at Fordragon Hold and the Horde's Kor'kron Vanguard prepare their assault. In the east the necropolis Naxxramas hangs above Wintergarde Keep, the Forsaken watch from Venomspite, and the Scarlet Onslaught has built a new Hearthglen on the coast. The Kalu'ak of Moa'ki, the homeless taunka and the Nerubians of Azjol-Nerub are caught in the middle of it all.

title: Coldwind Pass and Westwind
body: The only road from the Borean Tundra into the Dragonblight crosses a bridge at Coldwind Pass, where frozen elementals drift among the rocks and taunka braves keep watch for the caravans coming east. Wartook Iceborn waits at the bridge's end to meet them. A little way on lies the Westwind Refugee Camp, a cluster of tents where the Horde shelters taunka who have lost their homes. Among the broken families walks Emissary Brighthoof, a tauren sent north to look after her winter cousins, whom the refugees have taken as an elder. Two wounded blood guards, Roh'kill and Tor'zin, nurse their pride: the caravan they guarded to the camp was ambushed by Anub'ar in the woods to the east.

parts.body: Icemist is no more. The Scourge has fallen upon the taunka, and what fills these tents is all that remains of the taunka of the Borean Tundra and the Dragonblight: a broken people, battered and brought to the brink of extinction, whom the Horde means to nurse back to health so that they may strengthen it in turn.

title: Moa'ki Harbor
body: Moa'ki Harbor is the home of the Dragonblight Kalu'ak, tuskarr ruled by their chieftain, Elder Ko'nani. Turtle riders carry travelers between its docks and their kin at Unu'pe and Kamagua, and envoys of the Alliance and the Horde both wait on the elder. The harbor is not at peace. A great upheaval has just torn the land, and the wolvar of Snowfall Glade, crowded onto the glade to the north since outsiders came, raid the stores the Kalu'ak need for a journey whose end they do not yet know. Ko'nani speaks of the Dark One riding forth again and of the dragons' Nexus War. Trapper Mau'i holds that the wolvar have as much right to live as his own people.

parts.body: The wolvar raids were stopped the hard way. Loguhn, the Render of Flesh, alpha of the Snowfall Glade tribe, was slain before his hovel on the glade's northern rise, and his blood was worn back to Ko'nani as a sign of dominance and respect. The tribe now fights over his place, and the elder judges that it will have to be enough.
sources: quest 11959 description and reward text

parts.body: Toalu'u the Mystic sought the Kalu'ak's destiny from Oacha'noa, the sea goddess, called up with the Pearl of the Depths on the Briny Pinnacle. Her answer was that the Kalu'ak must stand with the outsiders. All souls are one with the magic of the world, the mystic says, and if the blue dragons win control of it, all are doomed. Elder Ko'nani accepts it, for weal or woe.

parts.body: Old Tua'kea the fisherman lost his crab traps to something far larger than a shark: Tu'u'gwar, He Who Plays With Food, his ancient nemesis, back in the harbor. Baited with the flesh of Kili'ua, the mother of all crabs from her island to the southwest, the beast took the hook and died, and Tua'kea is spreading the news to every Kalu'ak.

title: Indu'le Village
body: Indu'le was a Kalu'ak village on the high bluffs above Lake Indu'le, and Moa'ki has heard nothing from it since the ground shook and tore apart. What is left is a place of ghosts and madness. The spirits of its fishermen, warriors and mystics still walk the huts, and the villagers who lived through it wander among them out of their minds, attacking anyone who comes near. In the northwest corner stands the stone statue of Elder Mana'loa, one of the stone elders the tuskarr revere as fonts of ancient wisdom. Below, the lake itself has gone wrong: angry elementals churn in its waters.

parts.body: Elder Mana'loa told what happened. The sacred ground of the elves to the west was torn asunder, and its magic now runs through the land, ruining what it touches. The power came up through the lake and killed most of the village in an instant; those who survived were driven mad. He asked that the lingering spirits be set free to move on, and that the deranged living be left alone, for they may yet find their wits again.

title: Moonrest Gardens
body: Moonrest Gardens, in the far west of the Dragonblight, was the final resting place of a noble company of Highborne elves, and it lay on a ley line nexus. The blue dragonflight's mage hunters came with a giant device that now floats in the sky above the ruins, the Surge Needle, and bored a great pit into the gardens. The dead did not rest. The ghosts of the Highborne rose and slew half the mage hunters, whose bodies lie among the stones, and their spirits still prowl the ruins. Ethenial Moonshadow demands vengeance on the defilers. South of the gardens, more mage hunters hold the Glittering Strand.

parts.body: When the sorcerers bored their pit they let something loose: Arcanimus, a monstrosity that fed on the spirits of the dead. With Arcanimus destroyed, Ethenial gave a warning to carry to whoever would listen. By blowing apart the ley line anchor beneath the gardens, the blue dragonflight threatens to destroy them all.

parts.body: Not every mage hunter served willingly. On the Glittering Strand fell Captain Emmy Malin, and a letter in her robes told her father, Archmage Malin of Stormwind, that she had been forced to work for Malygos's armies under threat to her family, and was sabotaging them from within. At Stars' Rest, Commander Saia Azuresteel promised to see the letter delivered to him.

title: Stars' Rest
body: Stars' Rest is the Alliance's outpost in the west of the Dragonblight, held by night elves under Commander Saia Azuresteel with Sentinels on its paths. Its heart is a moonwell, from which Warden Jodi Moonsong draws the liquid fire of Elune to cleanse the beasts the Scourge has tainted around Icemist to the north. Palena Silvercloud keeps hippogryphs for riders, Sarendryana grieves for the ancients of the Lothalor Woodlands, and an image of Archmage Modera of the Kirin Tor speaks for Dalaran here, watching the blue dragonflight's work in the west.

parts.body: Courier Lanson, sent out from the Borean Tundra, reached Stars' Rest badly hurt. Anub'ar had ambushed him as he crossed the bridge into the Dragonblight, and they had known he was coming. He carries a list that must reach High Commander Halford Wyrmbane at Wintergarde Keep: the names of traitors in the Alliance's ranks. If any of them serve at Wintergarde, he warns, it could be catastrophic.

title: Lothalor Woodlands
body: The Lothalor Woodlands, between Stars' Rest and Agmar's Hammer, are the home of ancients, the most majestic of Northrend's children. The magic loosed across the land has reached them. Arcane wyrms have risen out of the ground and swarm through the trees, and some of the ancients have been corrupted and now strike at anything that moves. Only the treants of the woods seem untouched by it. Above the forest, mage hunters of the blue dragonflight guard another of their ley line foci, commanded by a troll lieutenant named Ta'zinni.

parts.body: Most of the ancients could still be saved. Fed the bark of the treants, who are immune to the magic, three of them were strengthened, and both camps took note. Sarendryana of Stars' Rest means to speak with them and ask for the Alliance's sake; Earthwarden Grife of Agmar's Hammer hopes to win them for the Horde, or at least to make them think twice about attacking it.

title: Icemist Village and the Pit of Narjun
body: Icemist Village, at the foot of the mountains west of Agmar's Hammer, was the capital of the taunka. Now it belongs to the Anub'ar, undead Nerubians of Azjol-Nerub. Their slayers and cultists fill the village, the cultists' suits leaking fumes that poison everything around them, and they are building an army of winged blightbeasts. In the middle of the village a taunka prisoner hangs in magical chains, cursing his captors. To the west gapes the Pit of Narjun, a vast sinkhole from which the Anub'ar marched to raze Icemist, and in its depths Nerubians who refuse the Lich King fight on.

parts.body: The Pit runs straight down to Azjol-Nerub, and the Horde feared the Anub'ar would use it to flank its army at the Wrathgate. So it struck first: a Warsong battle standard was planted in the middle of Icemist and held against all who came to tear it down. The Anub'ar were crushed by land, and the Horde vowed to crush them next by air.

title: Agmar's Hammer
body: Agmar's Hammer, a fortress of black, jagged metal in the west of the Dragonblight, is the Horde's testament to its power here, and Overlord Agmar rules it from his throne in Hellscream's name. Kor'kron guards walk its walls, Valnok Windrager's war riders circle above, and Captain Gort hunts traitors in its ranks. An image of Archmage Aethas Sunreaver speaks for the Kirin Tor beside the throne. Forsaken apothecaries under Doctor Sintar Malefious work in their own corner, to the disgust of Earthwarden Grife, and the unbound death knight Koltira Deathweaver has taken up residence for a time. Old Borus Ironbender, a smith of fifty years, broods over the Wrathgate's strange metal, which he swears he has seen breathe.

parts.body: The taunka have come to the Hammer. Armed by the Horde at Westwind, the refugees have made the trek east, and now taunka soldiers stand guard among the orcs. With them came Greatmother Icemist, who bears the name of the taunka's fallen village.

title: Wyrmrest Temple
body: Wyrmrest Temple, said to have been raised by the titans, stands at the center of the Dragonblight, and here the dragonflights confer in peace amidst the bones of their honored ancestors. It is the seat of the Wyrmrest Accord. Alexstrasza the Life-Binder holds court at its summit with her consort Krasus, beside Lord Itharius of the green flight, Chromie of the bronze, and Nalice of the black, who sneers at all of them and says they would never dare attack her there. Drakes carry visitors between its terraces, and the Alliance and the Horde each keep an ambassador at its foot. The peace has been broken: the blue dragonflight has launched a surprise attack on the temple itself.

parts.body: The queen abhors the loss of any life, but she will not let Malygos defile the temple. She named Lord Afrasastrasz commander of its defenses. From its middle terrace he sends riders out on Wyrmrest defenders to fight the blue dragons and drakes in the air, and to strike at the eruption of ley line energy at the Azure Dragonshrine, whose stolen power has emboldened the blues to attack the temple itself.

The magnataur of the wastes, who seldom gather without killing one another, had come together under a single warlord, carrying horns marked with a hammer and a lightning bolt. His name was won from the runemaster Dregmar Runebrand: Grom'thar the Thunderbringer. Called out with his own horn to the ring of torches south of the Azure Dragonshrine, he fell, and the magnataur were left to fight among themselves again.

title: The Ruby Dragonshrine
body: West of Wyrmrest, in a ring of scarred canyons, lies the Ruby Dragonshrine of the red dragonflight, a sacred place where a great tree drops ruby acorns and the ruby lilac grows. The Scourge has overrun it. Frigid necromancers work inside, the red wyrms that fell defending it rise again as skeletal emberwyrms, and ghouls, geists and abominations pour out through the canyons. Ruby keepers and guardians hold the ridges with the help of a regiment from each of the Alliance and the Horde. The shrine's keeper, Dahlia Suntouch, is nowhere to be found.

parts.body: Red dragons still fall in the battle overhead. To spare them from joining the emberwyrms, ruby acorns from the shrine's tree were planted beside their bodies, returning them to the earth, where they can give new life: a proud fate for any of their kind.

parts.body: Dahlia was found beneath the shrine. The Scourge had turned her into the source of its corruption, and only in death was she freed. Her lingering spirit told of falling at the feet of a death knight named Bloodbane, and warned that the Lich King now treads on the most sacred lands of every flight to force the dragons to act. The red dragons who heard it wondered what her fall means for the younger races, if one so devoted could be corrupted.

title: The Obsidian Dragonshrine
body: Northwest of Wyrmrest and just west of the Wrathgate, the Obsidian Dragonshrine of the black dragonflight smolders among the bones of its dead. The Cult of the Damned has come here too: necrolytes and their burning skeletons crowd the approach, and deeper in, in the cave called the Maw of Neltharion, the cultists draw power from the bones of fallen black dragons. One black dragon has come to deal with them, Serinar, who has played his part in destroying whole civilizations and is disgusted to stoop to the cult. At Wyrmrest, the black ambassador Nalice mocks the red flight for saving only its own shrine.

parts.body: The cult meant to make the black dragons its own. In the back of the Maw, Rothin the Decaying was raising the dead of Serinar's brood as magmawyrms, fed by necromantic runes drawn on the cave floor. The runes were stamped out, the bones in the summoning chamber were burned with Neltharion's Flame so that none could toy with them again, and Rothin was destroyed. Serinar relished every scream.

title: The Emerald Dragonshrine
body: On the southern shore of the Dragonblight lies the Emerald Dragonshrine, the garden of Ysera, kept by the green dragon Nishera. It is a living place among the bones: emerald lashers grow in it, great skytalons guard the sky above it, and green dragons are said to weep before they die, leaving hardened tears scattered through the shrine. Nishera warns visitors to watch their step, for things in the garden are not always as they seem. Even its defenders now treat outsiders as enemies.

parts.body: Nishera fears for the Dreamer. A horrible nightmare has taken hold in the Emerald Dream, and when she asked Ysera to help fight the Scourge raising frost wyrms at the other shrines, Ysera misunderstood and told the shrine's defenders to treat all who are not green dragons as enemies. The shrine has lost its balance, and its skytalons must be thinned to restore it.
sources: quest 12454 description

parts.body: Even that was not enough. Alystros, the immense skytalon who keeps the shrine's aerial defenses, would not listen to reason and had to be slain. Nishera bids no one weep for him: he has given his eternal life to the shrine's defense and will be reborn, free, she hopes, of the confusion of the Emerald Nightmare that grips the Dreamer.
sources: quest 12456 description and reward text

parts.body: Lord Itharius, the green ambassador at Wyrmrest, knows another of the shrine's properties: any unliving creature that steps into it falls to dust, save the Forsaken. Seeds of its lashers proved it, gravely weakening a reanimated frost wyrm, Turgid the Vile of the Carrion Fields and Overseer Deathgaze of Jintha'kalar. He means to ask Ysera's leave to use them, if she can be coaxed from her nightmare.

title: The Bronze Dragonshrine
body: In the east of the Dragonblight lies the Bronze Dragonshrine, and it is hidden in a storm of time. The storm keeps immortals out, and inside it the Infinite Dragonflight, strange bronze dragons of uncertain origin, battles the shrine's defenders for control of it. Chromie, the bronze flight's ambassador at Wyrmrest, has a plan: mortals can cross into the storm where her kind cannot, and with the Hourglass of Eternity they might learn who leads the Infinite.

parts.body: The hourglass did not reveal the Infinite Dragonflight's leader. It showed something Chromie found better: Nozdormu, the Lord of Time, alive and fighting the Infinite himself. No one had known where or when he had gone, only that he had disappeared to deal with very important matters.

title: Galakrond's Rest
body: North of Wyrmrest lie the dying grounds of Galakrond, the progenitor of dragonkind, whose bones are larger than all the Aspects together. The Scourge is digging them up. Scavengers labor day and night in the snow, rotting storm giants and frost wyrms guard the digs, and from the ridge of the Wicked Coil above them, Grand Necrolord Antiok rides the shoulders of Thiassi the Lightning Bringer, a reconstructed storm giant lord, and drives his workers on. His voice carries far: the Lich King, he shouts, demands more frost wyrms for Angrathar, and soon the bones of Galakrond will rise.

title: Nozzlerust Post and the Crystal Vice
body: In the north of the Dragonblight the goblins of Nozzlerust Post have found a war to profit from. Narf, Xink and Zivlix sell to anyone with coin: ore lifted from the Scourge digs, jormungar meat for hungry troops, lumber for the Alliance's towers, explosives carried by runners to the Wrathgate, when the harpies of Coldwind Heights do not catch them first. In the Crystal Vice to the northeast, crystalline ice giants under Ko'char the Unbreakable shelter from the dragons and fight jormungar that rise from the cavern below to eat them. Narf's brother Zort is there too, hoping to talk the giants into dying for the goblins.

parts.body: Ko'char never trusted the green runt. He fought his own war, and it ended in the Ice Heart Cavern with the death of Rattlebore, the jormungar spawnmother, a name gifted to her by an adventurer from the Plaguelands. The giant judged that some little ones have nobler intentions than goblins, and pointed the way north to Crystalsong, a cursed and dangerous place.

title: Fordragon Hold
body: Nestled against the mountain in the north of the Dragonblight, Fordragon Hold is the Alliance's base of operations against Angrathar the Wrathgate, and Highlord Bolvar Fordragon commands it in person. The hold is still being built around him: carpenters, masons and lumberjacks raise its walls while footmen drill at practice dummies. Knights and battle mages, marksmen and gryphon riders muster for the assault on the gate, and medics tend the wounded.

parts.body: When Wintergarde was saved, Lord Fordragon came back to Angrathar to prepare his forces for the destruction of the Wrathgate, and the hold grew busier for it: captains of Stormwind now stand among its soldiers.

title: The Kor'kron Vanguard
body: The Kor'kron Vanguard is the Horde's camp before the Wrathgate, the elite of the Warchief's guard come to break the Lich King's door. Kor'kron and Warsong elites, Darkspear spear throwers, taunka huntsmen and windfuries muster among war kodos and battle wyverns while peons keep the camp standing. Their commander is Saurfang the Younger, son of High Overlord Varok Saurfang. His father has gifted him his own battle armor and axe, and he means to put them to good use soon.

parts.body: The elder Saurfang sent a secret letter to Agmar's Hammer, slipped past the Overlord's readers by a messenger. The Horde's forces in Northrend serve under young Hellscream, he wrote, and every victory gives Hellscream's savage tactics more justification, leading the Horde back toward a dark place. So he sent his son to command at the Wrathgate, his heart and strength where he could not be, hoping the young orc's honor would be noticed and followed.

title: Angrathar the Wrathgate
body: Angrathar the Wrathgate is the barred entrance to Icecrown, a vast gate set into the mountains at the northern edge of the Dragonblight. The metal that holds it together pulses and shifts as if it were alive; old smiths swear they have seen it breathe. Before it lies the Court of Skulls, where the Alliance and the Horde fight side by side against the Scourge that pours out to meet them: aberrations, frail constructs and colossal abominations, plague eruptors, frenzied gargoyles and the necrolords who drive them. Frost wyrms strafe the field from above.

parts.body: Since the battle the field before the gate has fallen strangely still. The dead of the Scourge, the Alliance and the Horde lie where they fell, and Alexstrasza the Life-Binder and her consort Korialstrasz have come down from Wyrmrest to stand before the Wrathgate, looking over what remains.

title: Wintergarde
body: Wintergarde Keep holds the eastern border of the Dragonblight, the 7th Legion's fortress, and above it hangs the necropolis Naxxramas. The village that once lay below the keep is gone. Its ruins are now the Carrion Fields, a breeding ground of the Scourge, where plague wagons roll, siegesmiths build their engines and the hungering dead wander in their hundreds. Geists haunt the town square, the dead rise from the crypt, the mine has been lost, and risen gryphon riders strike from the sky. From Thorson's Post across the fields, the Legion's steam tanks wait for the order to advance.

parts.body: The Wintergarde Mine held a strange ore, and the Scourge now works it with the miners it has raised, to fuel its war machines. Slinkin the demo-gnome, sent in to learn more, died there, but the note in his hand told what he had overheard: the Scourge call the ore saronite, and speak the name Yogg-Saron with great contempt. His last wish was that both entrances be blown shut, so the evil inside could never get out.

title: New Hearthglen
body: On the cliffs of the southern coast, below Venomspite, the Scarlet Onslaught has built a new Hearthglen. It has walls and barracks, an abbey with a bell tower, a chapel, a smithy, stables and a lumbermill, and ballistae line its walls. Footmen and raven priests fill its streets, Forsaken prisoners rot in its cages, and the torturer LeCraft works in the barracks' basement. At Crusader's Landing below lies the Sinner's Folly, the Onslaught's flagship. High General Abbendis commands the town, with an admiral of the Scarlet Fleet named Barean Westwind close at hand.

parts.body: Venomspite cut off the Onslaught's retreat. Burning water brewed from the Forsaken blight set the Sinner's Folly's sails ablaze from the dock, and while the deckhands fought the fire, Captain Shely's rutters were taken from his cabin. Without them, the Onslaught has nowhere to run.

title: Venomspite
body: Venomspite is the Forsaken town in the east of the Dragonblight, on the south side of the mountain, where Vengeance Pass leads north to the Carrion Fields. High Executor Wroth commands it and has decreed death for every member of the Scarlet Onslaught to the south. Chief Plaguebringer Middleton runs its laboratory, promising to ravage the living, or rather, he corrects himself, the Scourge. Spy Mistress Repine runs agents, Apothecary Vicky Levine keeps starved rats, blight spreaders wait at the gate, and Quartermaster Bartlett complains that the Kor'kron at the Wrathgate have taken every coin in the coffers.

parts.body: Wroth knows the instruments of his trade. The rod of compulsion taken from the Onslaught's torturer was familiar to him from his youth, when he served as a torturer in the court of King Terenas of Lordaeron, and he put it to use at once on the Onslaught's own officers.

title: The Forgotten Shore
body: On the southeastern coast the Forgotten Shore is strewn with broken ships whose crews never left, and above the beach stand the ruins of an old Alliance base. Ghostly peasants, riflemen, footmen, knights and captains of the Alliance walk the beach and the waters off it, soldiers who have not understood that they are dead, crying out against a betrayal and a prince who gave them his word. Treasure still lies among the wrecks. Nearby at Dawn's Reach the Argent Crusade has made camp to quell the damned souls trying to escape Wintergarde, and the Forsaken of Venomspite eye the shore as a site for a new mausoleum.

title: Alexstrasza the Life-Binder
body: Alexstrasza the Life-Binder, Aspect of the red dragonflight, is the Queen of the Dragons, and from the summit of Wyrmrest Temple she leads the Wyrmrest Accord. She greets mortals as friends and tells them she has known them since before they were born. She abhors the loss of any life, yet her flight is at war on every side: Malygos has turned his blue dragons against the world's magic and against the temple itself, and the Scourge defiles the shrines and the bones of her kind. Mortals who reach her bring news, and ask her leave.

parts.body: The news of the ley lines explained a puzzle. She had wondered why the blue dragonflight dared to attack the temple so boldly, and now she knew: they are using enormous amounts of the very magic they claim is a threat to Azeroth. Hypocritical, she said, but so be it. If Malygos will not come to his senses, the Accord has no choice but to act.
sources: quests 12123 and 12124 reward text

parts.body: She cannot loose the full fury of the red dragonflight against the Scourge while her flight is entrenched in the war with Malygos. But the bravery of mortals never fails to astound her, rising to challenge death's cold stare, and it is why their kind is so loved, and so hated. To those who fight, she gives her blessing.

title: Korialstrasz
body: Korialstrasz is Alexstrasza's consort, and at Wyrmrest he stands beside her in the form he wore for years among the mages of Dalaran: Krasus, an elder of the Kirin Tor who sat on its ruling council. When the Dragonmaw held his queen captive in Grim Batol, it was he who worked to see her freed. Now the Scourge has overrun the Ruby Dragonshrine of his flight, and he calls on every ally he has to save it.

parts.body: The ruby brooch of Dahlia Suntouch came back to him from the fallen shrine. He grieved that she had been taken by the Scourge, and resolved to find a new keeper once the shrine is retaken. The Ruby Dragonshrine is sacred to his flight, he said, and the sacrifices made there will not be forgotten. He promised to call upon the one who brought the brooch one day.

title: Overlord Agmar
body: Overlord Agmar, commander of the Kor'kron in the Dragonblight, issues Hellscream's commands from the throne of Agmar's Hammer: his word, he says, is life and death. Two great worgs, Gar'mak and Lak'tuk, lie at his feet, and he trusts almost no one. Every letter in the Hammer passes through his hands before it is sent, for there are spies and traitors everywhere, and his wanted posters prove it: a mage commander of his own who went over to the blue dragonflight is marked for death beside the beasts that prey on his caravans. His eyes are on Angrathar.

parts.body: One letter amused him. A troll mage hunter, Lieutenant Ta'zinni, died with a note to his sister Deino in his robes: he had been forced to serve Malygos's armies under threat to his family, and was sabotaging them from within. Agmar laughed at it and called him a traitor. Yet he had known Deino once, a troll with honor, and promised she would learn her brother's fate, without learning who killed him. In return, he told the messenger, he owned them now.

title: Kilix the Unraveler
body: Kilix the Unraveler is a Nerubian of Azjol-Nerub who has not bowed to the Lich King, and he waits in the depths of the Pit of Narjun with a few battleguards. His kingdom is at war with itself. At the heart of the world, he says, the last living members of his species defend themselves against total annihilation, for the Lich King means to rule Azjol-Nerub at any cost, and those who will not yield are branded enemies of the Scourge and marked for death. He warns that the Pit is no place for the meek, and offers the Horde a common enemy in Arthas.

parts.body: Kilix knows the odds: there are thousands of the Anub'ar, spilling out of every dark crevice in Northrend, and no one stands a chance against them alone. Together, perhaps. As a gesture of good faith he sent Overlord Agmar a scroll setting out the strengths and weaknesses of the Nerubians attacking Icemist, and the overlord saw in it the means to crush the Anub'ar assault.

body: High Commander Halford Wyrmbane leads the 7th Legion at Wintergarde Keep. His soldiers are the nameless, faceless sons and daughters of the Alliance who fought through Mount Hyjal, the sands of Silithus and the armies of the Legion, and he holds that the first strike belongs to them and the last strike is all their enemies see. A plain-spoken soldier, he means to rebuild and fortify Wintergarde under the shadow of Naxxramas, and then to send reinforcements to Lord Fordragon at the Wrathgate.

title: High General Abbendis
body: High General Abbendis led the Scarlet Crusade in the Scarlet lands of Lordaeron and somehow survived the attacks upon Tyr's Hand. She brought a small force north, and on the coast of the Dragonblight founded New Hearthglen as the stronghold of the Scarlet Onslaught. Her soldiers carry copies of The Path of Redemption, said to hold her prophetic ramblings. Commander Eligor Dawnbringer of Wintergarde calls her his old enemy and believes she is far too shrewd an opponent to leave alive: whatever use her zealots might be against the Scourge, he is sure she will be at the Alliance's throat before the dust settles.

parts.body: Her journal tells how it began. A voice came to her in dreams, whispering 'Come to me', and she knew it for the Holy Light. Her breath misted in the warm sun as it spoke. A vision bade her take the most faithful and abandon the rest of the Crusade, and though she called herself a coward for it, she obeyed. Stepping onto the beach in Northrend, she planted her banner and proclaimed the Crimson Dawn: the Scarlet Crusade was no more, and the Scarlet Onslaught was born.

parts.body: Then a visitor came. Admiral Barean Westwind, who by all accounts had died on these shores an age ago, appeared at her door looking far too young for it, claiming the Light had kept him alive and sent him to be her advisor. Her men took to him with zeal, the high abbot took up a new blessing from him, and some of the men became raven priests. Abbendis could not make herself trust him, and the Light had fallen silent.

title: Into the Fold
body: The Horde means to bring the taunka into its ranks, and a tauren, Emissary Brighthoof, waits among the refugees at Westwind to welcome them into the fold. She will not send them out defenseless. The armaments meant for the Horde's newest members were lost when the Anub'ar ambushed a caravan from Agmar's Hammer in the woods east of the camp, and only two of its guards came back alive. The arms must be recovered from the Nerubians before the ceremony of initiation can begin.

parts.body: With Horde arms to lift their spirits, the taunka were ready. Each spoke the sacred words of the blood oath of the Horde, scroll in hand, and swore to give all they had to drive the Scourge from the world. They had nothing left, Brighthoof said; now they had purpose, and with purpose came hope. The new members of the Horde marched east to Agmar's Hammer.

title: The Stolen Ley Lines
body: On the morning the land of the western Dragonblight shook and tore apart, the Kirin Tor took notice. Images of Archmage Modera at Stars' Rest and Archmage Aethas Sunreaver at Agmar's Hammer summoned help in all haste, sure the upheaval would have broader repercussions than troubling the natives. Its source was Moonrest Gardens, a ley line nexus. The blue dragonflight had used a device called a surge needle to destroy it, freeing its power to be redirected at their will, and the archmages want to know where that power is going.

parts.body: The plans taken from the dead mage hunters showed the blue dragonflight seeking an accord with the Ethereum, the ethereals, who could be a powerful ally for Malygos and his madness. Wind Trader Mu'fah and the blue dragon Goramosh, who were to settle it in the gardens, were slain, but too late: Goramosh had let slip that the accord was already reached.

The blue flight uses it to find and destroy the anchors of the ley lines and send their power to the Nexus. But here the path of destruction ran east, when it should have run west.

The archmages saw at once what they should have guessed all along, and sent word that Wyrmrest must be warned.

title: Naxxramas and the Fall of Wintergarde
body: Lord Fordragon led a crushing assault against the Lich King's forces at the Wrathgate, and the Lich King answered by sending Naxxramas down upon Wintergarde. While Kel'Thuzad hides in the floating citadel, his ground commander, Thel'zan the Duskbringer, lays siege to the keep. The lower village is already lost, and every minute lessens the chance of pulling survivors from its ruins. High Commander Halford Wyrmbane needs every soldier he has, and gryphon riders are going out over the Carrion Fields to snatch up whoever still lives.

parts.body: Gryphon riders swept low over the Carrion Fields, once the village below the keep, and plucked helpless villagers from among the Scourge. Those who were saved were put back to work fortifying Wintergarde, and Halford hopes it will soon be strong enough to send reinforcements to Lord Fordragon at the Wrathgate.

Beneath the old village, Godfrey revealed, lay a mausoleum, and there Thel'zan hid and sent a thousand thousand corpses against the keep.

title: The Forgotten Tale
body: Zelig the Visionary hears the cries of the fallen echo across Northrend from his tower at Wintergarde Keep. Arthas left a terrible imprint on everything he touched, he says, and only wither and decay remain in his wake. Zelig holds that the past must be studied so the enemy can be better known, for untold truths might surface that could help the Alliance's campaign. First, though, his scrying orb must be recovered from the town hall in Wintergarde's embattled town square.

parts.body: The orb pointed south, to an atrocity committed long ago on the Forgotten Shore. There, at Dawn's Reach, Zelig's old friend Orik Trueheart of the Argent Crusade brewed an elixir of murkweed that let a living soul walk among the dead. The ghosts did not know the truth, Orik wept: they think Arthas a hero, when it was Arthas who ordered their ships burned and left them to die in this frozen land. Orik was only a lad in the prince's fleet, and he survived.

A map taken from the Scarlet Onslaught marked a cave by that name near Scarlet Point, and at its bottom Zelig's orb showed the past: Arthas taking up the cursed blade against Muradin's warnings, and Muradin struck down, waking with no memory of who he was. Muradin might yet live, Zelig dared to hope, and King Bronzebeard had to be told at once.

title: The Forsaken Blight
body: After an eternity of failure the plaguebringers of New Agamand have perfected their blight, and a specimen has come by bat to Chief Plaguebringer Middleton at Venomspite, who rejoices at the whole field of Scourge waiting beyond the mountain. At Agmar's Hammer, Doctor Sintar Malefious waits for it impatiently, calling it a Horde imperative, the last piece of the victory puzzle. First it must be made safe to handle. Middleton has synthesized an inert strain; mixed with a reactive agent, it would turn anyone near it into a shapeless pile of goo.

parts.body: The reactive agent came from the dead: ectoplasm of the Alliance specters haunting the beach to the south. The shell for the blight came from the Emerald Dragonshrine: the hardened tears that green dragons weep before they die.

title: The Spy in New Hearthglen
body: High Executor Wroth of Venomspite has decreed death for every member of the Scarlet Onslaught, the most zealous of the old Crusade, now dug in at New Hearthglen to the south. No quarter is offered, and any of his own taken by the humans will be left to their fate. Before Venomspite strikes, Spy Mistress Repine means to learn what the Onslaught is planning: its daily orders, from the abbey, the barracks and the beach, are to be stolen and put in her hands.

parts.body: The Forsaken found a strange thing. Their perfected blight, said to kill everything it touched, did nothing to a captured Onslaught soldier. Something protects them, and Apothecary Vicky Levine, horrified, had to fall back on starving rats to keep their priests from raising the dead.

parts.body: Repine had an agent inside the town all along: Agent Skully, disguised by magic as the Onslaught's cemetery caretaker. The stolen orders hinted that something was imminent, but first the Onslaught's strange protection had to be explained. title: The Battle for the Wrathgate
body: At Angrathar the Wrathgate the Alliance and the Horde stand side by side. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon holds Fordragon Hold and Saurfang the Younger the Kor'kron Vanguard, and together they have pressed the Scourge hard. But the Scourge does not relent. Frost wyrms strafe the field from above, and no advance on the gate itself is possible while they fly. They are made from the bones of ancient dragons, so before anyone defiles those bones, the dragon queen at Wyrmrest must give her leave.

parts.body: Alexstrasza warned that the wyrms were the least of their concerns. North of Wyrmrest lie the dying grounds of Galakrond, progenitor of dragonkind, from whom the titans created the Aspects, a beast larger than all the Aspects combined. The Scourge is digging up his bones, and Grand Necrolord Antiok commands the work from atop the Wicked Coil. Should the Scourge raise Galakrond, everything the armies at the gate have done would be for naught.
sources: quests 12495 and 12496 reward text

parts.body: On the back of a Wyrmrest vanquisher, a champion of the Accord burned the scavengers at Galakrond's Rest and struck down Antiok on the Wicked Coil, taking the scythe with which he controlled the wyrms. The queen declared that the deed had saved the armies at the gate from certain death, and had it recorded for posterity.
sources: quest 12498 description and reward text

parts.body: Bolvar and Saurfang the Younger led their armies against the gate together. The Lich King came out to meet them, Frostmourne in hand, promising the justice of the grave. Saurfang charged him, and the blade shattered his axe and slew him in a single stroke, taking his soul. Bolvar stood his ground.
sources: quests 12499 and 12500 reward text
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Battle_of_Angrathar_the_Wrathgate (the cinematic)

parts.body: Then Grand Apothecary Putress appeared on the heights above, crying that the Forsaken had not forgotten or forgiven, and his catapults rained plague on the field: death to the Scourge, and death to the living. Scourge, Alliance and Horde fell alike, and the Lich King himself staggered and withdrew behind his gate. The red dragonflight came down and burned the plague away, and with it the field, and Bolvar Fordragon fell amid the fire.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Battle_of_Angrathar_the_Wrathgate (Putress's words, the plague, the Lich King falling to his knees and retreating, the red flight incinerating the plague)

parts.body: Saurfang's battle armor was carried from the field to his father at Warsong Hold. The old orc looked to the heavens. Like Brox, he said, his son died a hero, and for an orc there could be no better end. The armor would be placed on his pyre at the Ancestral Grounds of Nagrand, and Varok turned his mind to more pressing matters.
